lines: Decision needed from Brandon, unchanged, one thing only he can do: the automation that restarts this build ends Friday noon Mountain Time and a run may not move its own end. He can move the end to Sunday noon in the automation's settings, or write any line in the thread. The Partner raises it again Friday morning. Open item 252.

Chain 25 is read whole and on origin main (`ade42c8f`, pushed 08:59 UTC): summer's glass fourth list, fall's air sixth list, summer's sand sixth list and summer's miniature fifth list. On it: tsc exit 0, build exit 0, engine `afc909cca25eb67b`; "pass M3 summer-rest: 0.8026" (base 0.803, miniature 0.823); "pass M3 fall-rest: 0.8047" (base 0.805, miniature 0.849); M4 0.9694, 0.8676, 0.9562, 0.9586 and M5 0.9934, 1, 0.9794, 0.9996, all pass; four of the eight draft stills moved, summer's two and fall's two, as they should; the whole vitest 68 files passed and 1 skipped, 947 tests passed and 4 skipped; `node tools/miniatures.mjs` pass; triangles at high winter 1,490,555, spring 1,453,115, summer 1,703,969, fall 1,799,613 of 1,800,000.

Chain 26 is running since 09:01 UTC on four more merges, not on origin yet: summer's tree tenth pass (`524cc65b`), fall's base tenth step (`0f7d05f9`), spring's base sixth list (`2237fa3a`) and fall's scene seventh list (`671968d3`). Read so far: tsc exit 0, five makes exit 0, build exit 0, engine `85cf73c2c01e9f16`; "pass M3 summer-rest: 0.8026" with the base at 0.803 and the miniature at 0.888 (0.823 before the tree's tenth pass); "pass M3 fall-rest: 0.8741" with the base at 0.913 (0.805 before the tenth step) and the miniature at 0.874; "pass M3 spring-rest: 0.8666" with the base at 0.909 and the miniature at 0.867. The change measure, stills, counts and the whole vitest are still running, done about 09:25 UTC.

Picture 1 is summer at rest on chain 26, the approved picture left and the build right. New in it: the crown is open, pads of leaves on boughs with sky between, where the ninth pass was one closed mass; its builder counts 21.3% open inside the outline where the approved has 29.4 and the ninth had 9.7 (STATED). Below the bar still, the crown by its builder's own word: the openings are four large ones and eight specks where the approved has many small ones, and the top light is a wide pale band where the approved has a thin line of yellow leaves. And as before: the seeds are of one size; the lights are even discs; a broad pale wash lies over the upper glass where the approved has thin arcs at the rim; the base carries soft bands; the stream of sand is a thin pale line. The eleventh pass of the tree deals the openings.

Picture 2 is spring at rest on chain 26 with the base's sixth list, the approved picture left and the build right. New: the moss cap is thick and rises round the glass, so the glass sits in the moss and the brown ring is gone. Below the bar by its builder's own measure: the body is too tall and upright (table to moss line 0.385 of the glass's diameter where the approved has 0.334, widest in the middle where the approved widens toward the table); at 3840 the lit moss is a smooth pale skin where the approved's is speckled; the trickle is a dark ribbon. The deep blue pixels and the hard red and white edges on the thin roots that rough draft 6 showed are being traced now; the builder's first reading, not yet a finding, is a gain on the low sun that puts those faces far over white.

Picture 3 is fall at rest on chain 26 with the scene's seventh list and the base's tenth step, the approved picture left and the build right. New: the roof reads as rows of single shingles, the fence posts are thinner (8 to 9 pixels where the approved has 7 to 8 and main had 12 to 14, STATED), the left of the base carries round vines. Below the bar: the air is thinner and greyer than the approved's haze (the seventh list of the air is in work, not in this picture); no lights along the boughs; the wall reads as round cobbles with wide joints where the approved has small flat blocks; the chimney's part of the measure fell from 0.83 to 0.68 by its builder's count; the left vines read as polished copper.

Picture 4 is fall's lit stone at 3840 at six times: the approved picture, the tenth step, and two tries, not pushed. It overturned an order of mine. I had ordered the grain made shallower because the stone read as static at full size. The builder measured first: the approved's lit stone is not smooth, it is a fine even pebble of pale dots on a lit grey ground (step at one pixel 22.9 where ours is 15.3 to 17.0), and ours is blotchier on near black (step over blocks of 4 pixels 23 to 26 where the approved has 16.1, median 47 where the approved has 106). At six times I see the same: ours are blobs two to three times as wide with black between. Try 1, my order, ends the static by eye and reads as soft blue cloth, further from the approved by measure. Ruled at 09:06 UTC: not the quick one; the stone goes toward the approved's own pebble on its own numbers, the lift only where the key light strikes, and film frames 2364 to 2367 at 3840 decide whether so fine a grain holds in motion. About 40 minutes more. Below the bar.

Two corrections. Status 205 said the controls' report on its second job was still owed; it came at 08:39 UTC and names no failure (the five arrays the same bytes whole and in steps, the two walks with nothing not ok, STATED); the hint is still late behind this renderer's stalls, and nothing is seen on a real card at 60 a second. Not a pass. And summer's base builder corrected its own pair of 08:51 UTC at 09:04 UTC: its boxes were not laid on each other (our globe stands 18.8 pixels lower in the frame), so the pale band above the big edge is 15 to 20 over the approved's and not 40 to 60 as it first said. My ruling stood in form; nothing had gone on from the wrong numbers.

Decision 184: a season may draw its own copy of the fence with its own widths and tops, as long as every post stands on the layout's feet and the count is the layout's. I read the roof's cover and the wall's stones the same way and told fall's scene builder so in its eighth list (6 rows of wider shingles where it has 8 narrow ones, wall stones at the approved's width as flat blocks, the chimney's shading mended first, a ring of warm stones over the door, the litter's red down on its own numbers); push about 10:30 UTC.

Other rulings since 08:39 UTC, each on the builder's own numbers. Fall's air, first pair of the seventh list: the bright points now count 557 where the approved has 572 (were 308); they read as beads of one size, each with the same orange ring; ruled that the ring goes and not the points, tied to the point's size, and the sizes dealt to the approved's spread; push about 09:40 UTC. Summer's glass, first pair of the fifth list: thin cream arcs at the upper left where one band lay; asked for two cuts along the radius counting the turns from light to dark before the bands are dealt; push about 09:30 UTC. Summer's base, the shelves pair: the upper left strata as hairlines where ours are soft stripes joined into one dark band, short broken ridges below the shell row where ours are long smooth bands; push about 09:20 UTC. Summer's air (seeds at rest and the landing) pushes about 09:20 UTC after mending a leak into fall's two stills that its own proof caught.

The sixth publish is not out, and the time Status 205 gave for it, about 09:15 UTC, is not kept. By the fifth publish's own times a publish holds this machine for 40 to 45 minutes (20 of them to draw the 40 first pictures the page shows before the app has drawn), and four pushed parts were waiting, so chain 26 went first. The plan now: when chain 26 is read and pushed, a helper machine draws the 40 first pictures from that head while this machine reads the next chain; then the build, the checks, the security review and the publish. About 10:30 UTC. The live app is still the fifth publish.

4K motion: the shutter's builder is to draw chunk 58 of film B (frames 1740 to 1769, summer) at 3840 with the masters' settings on chain 25's head as a first whole test of motion, with every neighbouring pair measured and a one to one crop played six times. Fall at speed waits for the stone. Not a pass.

Render counts since the last status. Drawn here: chain 25's eight stills, its counts and the whole vitest; chain 26's three measure stills. On helper machines: the builders' own stills and looks. No frame of the masters yet.
Sound: 7,420 of 10,000 credits, unchanged, no call planned.
